title: The Koto II experiment
summary: $K_L \rightarrow π^0ν\barν$ is a golden mode for flavour physics: it is highly suppressed in the Standard Model, with a predicted branching ratio of $3 \times 10^{-11}$ and a theoretical uncertainty of just 2\%, and is therefore extremely sensitive to new physics. The KOTO experiment at J-PARC is searching for this decay. Using the data taken in 2021, it has set the most stringent upper limit to date of $2.2 \times 10^{-9}$ on the branching ratio at 90\% C.L. We present KOTO II, a next-generation experiment at J-PARC proposed in 2024, which aims to measure the $K_L \rightarrow π^0ν\barν$ branching ratio with a sensitivity below $10^{-12}$ in the 2030s.

title: GeoRead: Geometry-Aware Transformer for Continuous AC-LGAD Readout Reconstruction
summary: AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) are promising silicon sensor technologies for high-precision four-dimensional tracking. Position reconstruction in AC-LGADs relies on correlations among waveforms induced on multiple readout pads, where analytically solving the signal propagation becomes difficult, motivating data-based machine learning reconstruction. Existing machine learning approaches generally assume a fixed readout pad layout and predict one hit from an isolated, temporally aligned waveform window. These assumptions limit their flexibility across sensor designs and applicability to continuous readout where signal arrival times are not known in advance and multiple hits might overlap in the same waveforms. We introduce GeoRead, a spatial-temporal Transformer enabling multi-event continuous position prediction and uncertainty estimation. We incorporate relative pad positions into attention and produces time-resolved hit position estimates with predictive uncertainties. Time-jitter and additive event-mixing augmentations are used to train the model on temporally misaligned and overlapping waveforms synthesized from single-event measurements. Using four-channel transient-current-technique (TCT) data of a 500\mum-pitch AC-LGAD, GeoRead achieves median position errors of 5.8\mum within the convex hull of the readout-pad centers and 8.2\mum over the full scanned region at 190\volt. The model maintains comparable accuracy under temporal shifts and demonstrates time-resolved reconstruction of superposed events, without predefined per-event window. These results provide a basis for extending waveform-based position reconstruction toward continuous readout and flexible sensor geometries.

title: Kinematic Reconstruction of Top-Quark Pairs Using Analytical and Machine-Learning Methods with CMS Open Data
summary: The reconstruction of the top-quark-pair ($t\bar{t}$) kinematics in the dilepton $t\bar{t}$ decay channel is challenging due to the presence of two undetected neutrinos. In this work, existing kinematic reconstruction methods used by the CMS Collaboration are studied using a Monte Carlo sample with $t\bar{t}$ events from CMS Open Data at a centre-of-mass energy of 7 TeV. An improved version of the loose kinematic reconstruction, LKRv2, is developed by imposing more stringent requirements on the jet-lepton pairing entering the reconstruction. A further modification, LKRv3, exploits the kinematic similarity between the dilepton and neutrino-pair systems and improves the resolution of the reconstructed $t\bar{t}$ invariant mass relative to the baseline LKR by $7\%$, with smaller improvements for the transverse momentum and rapidity of $t\bar{t}$. In addition, two machine-learning (ML) based approaches are developed using a residual multilayer perceptron and a conditional normalizing flow. Relative to LKRv3, they improve the resolution of the invariant mass, transverse momentum and rapidity by approximately $30\%$, $20\%$ and $15\%$, respectively. In particular, a resolution of 30 GeV is achieved for the reconstructed invariant mass of $t\bar{t}$ near the production threshold. A dedicated generator-level study and a generator-to-detector transfer test demonstrate that the ML approaches learn a genuine physics-driven correction to the $ν\barν$ approximation, rather than merely exploiting detector-specific effects. These results demonstrate the strong potential of ML-based approaches for improving the reconstruction of dilepton $t\bar{t}$ events, while identifying the neutrino-pair approximation as an important limitation on the achievable resolution.

title: Observing Transverse Momentum Broadening from TEECs in Heavy Ion Collisions
summary: We study the azimuthal dependence of transverse energy-energy correlators (TEECs) in dijet events in heavy-ion collisions. In the back-to-back region this observable resolves the energy flow around $φ=π$ and is sensitive to medium-induced momentum broadening and the response of the medium. To isolate final-state effects, we consider a quark-antiquark pair produced in a colour-singlet hard process and propagating through a homogeneous background medium. Starting from the vacuum TMD factorization formula, we combine NLL$'$ resummation with medium modifications at first order in the strong coupling. For the parameters studied, (classical) momentum broadening lowers the back-to-back peak and leaves the distribution elsewhere nearly unchanged, while radiative corrections significantly suppress the peak further and enhance larger angular decorrelations. We additionally include the medium response sourced by each jet, as a mean energy flow. This spreads the deposited energy over the whole azimuth, so that the contribution to the TEEC varies slowly across the back-to-back region, is small at the peak and grows toward larger angles.

title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
comment: 65 pages, 6 figures. Lean 4 formalization is available at https://github.com/stacks-ai/papers/tree/main/conley-index-dynamical-systems
summary: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $Δ(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+ε)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.

title: Transformer-Based Characterization of Criticality in Directed Percolation
summary: Directed percolation (DP) provides a canonical framework for studying nonequilibrium phase transitions into absorbing states, yet extracting critical behavior directly from high-dimensional spatiotemporal configurations remains challenging. Here, we investigate (1 + 1)- and (2 + 1)-dimensional bond DP using a supervised Transformer encoder. Supervised learning results demonstrate that the Transformer can distinguish between the active and absorbing phases of directed percolation with high accuracy. The critical point and critical exponents estimated from the model's classification probabilities align closely with reference values from existing literature, indicating that the model not only achieves phase classification but also yields outputs containing information related to critical scaling behavior. To probe the model's internal representation, we employ attention rollout and define an attention center that quantifies the temporal centroid of the cumulative attention distribution. The attention patterns and the attention center reorganize systematically near the critical region and exhibit pronounced finite-size dependence. Finally, we examined the model's transferability between configurations generated from fully occupied initial states and those from single-seed initial states. The results indicate the presence of transferable information between the two types of data, though the transfer performance exhibits directional asymmetry. Furthermore, when using an equal amount of target-domain data, fine-tuning yielded only a marginal improvement in accuracy compared to training from scratch.

title: The Kähler Stability Wall in Perturbative Brane--Antibrane Inflation
comment: 22 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables, Comments are Welcome!
summary: Perturbative brane--antibrane inflation requires the physical Kähler volume to remain stabilized while the anti-D3 sector supplies the inflationary energy. This paper shows that this requirement imposes an exact analytic boundary on the allowed anti-D3 tension. In the leading nilpotent effective theory, the Kähler minimum and the decompactification barrier disappear through a saddle-node degeneration determined by \(U_σ=U_{σσ}=0\). The positive-tension branch of this boundary is solved in closed form and uniformized by a single real parameter. The same solution fixes the local scaling of the Kähler mass, barrier height, and canonical distance to the endpoint. Integrating out the volume modulus reveals a Schur-complement singularity, showing that the adiabatic single-field description fails at the same boundary unless the inflaton--volume mixing is suppressed. The result is then translated into necessary flux-arithmetic filters involving the warped throat, D3 tadpole, conifold control, scalar normalization, and the full Kähler-sector mass matrix. Numerical tests verify the critical locus, the saddle-node scaling laws, and the resulting sparse throat-flux filtration. These conditions are necessary for compact realizations; no compact vacuum is asserted without the corresponding global and Wilsonian control checks.

title: Constraints on Quintom Dark Energy Model with Matter Interaction
summary: The quintom model consisting of quintessence and phantom scalar fields with linear coupling to matter is explored and constrained by updated DESI and supernovae type Ia~(SNIa) observational data. The matter interaction is assumed only between phantom and matter and the quintessence self potential is in an exponential form. The quintom evolution shows a class of solutions with phantom crossing scenario consistent with the current DESI data. From low redshift observations, we place constraints on the model with BAO data from DESI and distance measurements from SNIa Pantheon+ samples and SH0Es. For high-redshift constraints, we use CMB priors from Planck and found that the quintom model gives the best-fit Hubble parameter $H_{0}=65.780~(68.736)$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ for DESI+CMB+SNIa~(+SH0ES) respectively. The marginalized statistical constrained values are $H_{0}=66.21\pm 0.84~(68.49^{+0.46}_{-0.40})$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ for DESI+CMB+SNIa~(+SH0ES) respectively. Using the BBN prior for high-redshift constraints, the corresponding best-fit values for DESI+BBN+SNIa~(+SH0ES) constraints are $H_{0}=63.999~(71.962)$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and the marginalized statistical values for DESI+BBN+SNIa~(+SH0ES) constraints are $H_{0}=61.6^{+6.6}_{-3.0}~(71.86\pm 0.88)$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ respectively. Generally, adding SH0ES significantly raises the best-fit and marginalized value of $H_{0}$ for all datasets. In comparison to $Λ$CDM, the interacting quintom model gives lower values of $σ_{8}=0.74-0.79$ for combination of datasets with CMB prior. Lastly, the fifth-force constraint from local scale solar system Cassini probe is estimated, we find the constraint on the phantom-matter coupling $|δ|<3.3\times 10^{-3}$.

title: Magic Is in the Eye of the Measure
summary: Magic, or nonstabilizerness, is the quantum resource behind universal quantum computation. Its applications in high-energy and nuclear physics rely almost exclusively on the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), although magic has no unique measure. For two qubits, we compare the SRE with three measures defined through optimizations over stabilizer states: the min- and max-relative entropies of magic and the logarithmic free robustness. We determine the maximal-magic states of all four measures, with exact proofs, and find that they depend on the measure. In the determination of the weak mixing angle from minimal magic in Møller scattering, the min-relative entropy gives an energy-dependent value that differs from that of the SRE, whereas the max-relative entropy and the logarithmic free robustness give $\sin^2θ_W=1/4$ at all energies. We trace this difference to the non-analytic structure of the optimization-based measures. Physical conclusions drawn from extremizing magic can thus depend on the measure.

title: Standard Subspaces and Modular Theory -- General Theory and Applications to QFT
comment: Work in progress, comments are welcome. 143 pages
summary: This is a preview of an upcoming monograph on standard subspaces and modular theory. At the moment, it consists of the first chapter. This starts with a gentle introduction to the subject, and then describes the modular theory of standard subspaces, the characterization of their modular data by the KMS condition and reflection positivity, and various constructions of standard subspaces. Further topics in Chapter 1 include the connection of standard subspaces to complexifications and symplectic structures, including their polarizers, and operations with standard subspaces, namely direct sums, direct integrals, and tensor products. Many examples and classification results are included as well. This first chapter also contains a description of the free U(1)-current and some other applications to quantum field theory, such as KMS states of type I factors, the local subspaces of the free Klein--Gordon field, and the entropy operator defined by a standard subspace.

title: Nonequilibrium Fluctuations and Intrinsic Stability of Nanostructured Solar Cells: Microscopic Derivation and Universal Laws
summary: We study nonequilibrium fluctuations of efficiency in nanostructured solar cells. Our contribution is threefold. First, we derive a microscopic stochastic model of efficiency from a two-state master equation describing absorption, radiative recombination, and extraction. This derivation establishes an explicit link between efficiency fluctuations and entropy production, and justifies the thermodynamic affinity through local detailed balance. Second, we review universal fluctuation laws established in the recent literature and apply them for the first time to the real parameters of nanostructured solar cells. We show that the total entropy production behaves as a submartingale, and that its negative exponential is a martingale. For a biased discrete random walk, the exact infimum law is verified numerically in the near-equilibrium regime, then applied to realistic solar cell configurations. Third, our simulations show that nanostructured solar cells operate in a strongly nonequilibrium regime, where negative entropy fluctuations, and hence efficiency fluctuations, are exponentially rare. Over all simulated trajectories, most configurations show no detectable negative fluctuation, consistent with the theoretical prediction. These results explain the intrinsic statistical stability of the devices and provide a conceptual and quantitative framework for understanding efficiency fluctuations around the mean values. They do not modify the mean efficiencies obtained previously, but clarify their statistical robustness in the strongly nonequilibrium regime.

authors: Lucas Ducastelo de C. C. Lima
title: Explicit Symmetry Breaking in Non-Abelian Scalar Theories and One-Loop Renormalization
summary: Non-Abelian gauge theories coupled to scalar fields are fundamental in particle physics, yet they often face high-energy instabilities. In this work, we start by analyzing the classical $SU(2)$ complex scalar model, mapping the scalar multiplet into a real $SO(2N)$ representation to formalize its generalization to $SU(N)$. Within this classical setup, we introduce an explicit gauge symmetry breaking exclusively in the scalar sector by splitting the mass parameters and quartic self-coupling constants. Moving to the quantum level, we employ the background field method and the Schwinger-DeWitt technique to compute the exact one-loop divergences, explicitly demonstrating the renormalizability of the broken theory. Finally, we derive the Renormalization Group equations and analyze the fixed points of the flow. It is shown that this explicit symmetry breaking asymptotically destabilizes the theory, driving the scalar couplings away from the origin and inevitably leading to a Landau pole.

title: Phentax: A JAX implementation of the IMRPhenomTHM waveform model
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, submitted to the `Journal of Open Source Software.`
summary: The upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to be sensitive to thousands of white dwarf (WD) binaries in our galaxy, extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) of stellar-mass compact objects into massive black holes, stellar-mass black hole binaries (SOBHBs) in their early inspiral phase, and, crucially, massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) with masses in the range of $10^4$-$10^7 M_\odot$. The presence of such a large number of signals requires joint inference of all parameters across all sources present in the data, an approach referred to as "global fit". This requires evaluating hundreds of thousands of waveform templates, which can be computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we present $\texttt{Phentax}$, a $\texttt{JAX}$ re-implementation of the $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ waveform model. This is a state-of-the-art time-domain phenomenological waveform model for comparable-mass binary black holes that includes the effects of higher-order modes. Given this, $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ is one of the models currently used to simulate and analyze MBHB signals in LISA. With $\texttt{Phentax}$, we provide a fast, easy-to-batch, and differentiable implementation of this waveform model to accelerate the development of LISA global fit algorithms.

title: Just CaloCHILL: fast hadronic shower generation in a learned latent space
comment: 25 pages, 19 figures, 11 tables. Code: https://github.com/FLC-QU-hep/CaloCHILL, data: https://doi.org/10.25592/uhhfdm.22077
summary: Calorimeter showers are the most expensive part of detector simulation, and highly granular calorimeters, in which a single hadronic shower leaves thousands of energy deposits, make them more expensive still. We present CaloCHILL (Calorimeter Hits In Learned Latents), a generative model that does not produce these deposits one by one: instead it generates a compact summary of the shower in a learned latent space and expands it to full resolution only at the end. The complete shower, including the arrival time of every hit, is built in three stages: a flow-matching model first sets the number of hits and the earliest hit time in each calorimeter layer, a mean-flow model then generates the latent summary, and the decompressor of a variational autoencoder turns it into the full point cloud, giving every hit its position, energy and time. Sparse attention along the shower axis keeps this compression affordable for showers with thousands of hits. On positive-pion showers in the calorimeter of the International Large Detector, a proposed detector for the FCC-ee, CaloCHILL reproduces the main shower observables, including their time structure. This new model is 600 times faster than its predecessor, while improving on all accuracy metrics considered.

title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation
summary: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schrödinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.

title: Permutation order governs basin entropy in critical one-input Boolean networks
summary: Basin entropy measures uncertainty about a network's long-term behavior. For every critical one-input synchronous Boolean network with $m$ relevant nodes, we show that the permutation structure induced by its feedback loops determines basin entropy, up to a universal error. Although the loops oscillate independently, their relative phases can be offset, producing a deviation from additivity that can grow linearly in $m$. Yet at the ensemble level, a previously derived additive prediction is preserved through the first subleading term, with the discrepancy appearing at order $\ln m\ln\ln m$.

title: Andreev reflections and optimal truncation in the unitary Fermi droplet
summary: We study the unitary Fermi gas in an external trap in the double-scaling limit of large flavor number N and large charge Q at fixed Q/N. At leading order, the problem reduces to the spectral zeta function of a BdG operator in an inhomogeneous pairing background. The grand potential admits a gradient expansion with distinct bulk and edge sectors. We show that when the trap is harmonic, the bulk sector expansion terminates: beyond the first three terms every bulk contribution integrates to zero. This cancellation is general and follows from zeros of the Euler beta function computed in the Son-Wingate effective field theory, independent of the low-energy constants. The truncation persists for anisotropic traps in any odd dimension. All higher-order dependence for harmonic potentials is therefore carried by the droplet edge. For anharmonic traps, the asymptotic bulk series is factorially divergent. Using a heat-kernel WKB analysis, we show that its large-order growth, sign oscillations, and optimal truncation are fixed by complex periodic orbits of the BdG problem, which are analytic continuations of Andreev reflections. We numerically confirm the predicted Borel singularities for quartic and sextic traps.

title: Effects of Self-Interactions on the Bifurcations in Boson Stars
summary: Radially excited mini-boson stars have zero modes under static axisymmetric perturbations, at which they bifurcate into axisymmetric configurations with chain-like and ring-like matter distributions. We study how self-interactions affect the $\ell=2$ zero modes of spherical boson stars with one radial node, and construct the chains and rings that bifurcate from them. We consider massive and solitonic boson stars, which have a repulsive quartic self-interaction and a Q-ball type potential, respectively. For massive boson stars, the zero mode persists for all values of the quartic coupling we considered. As the coupling grows, it moves onto the candidate stable branch, so that this branch cannot be entirely stable against $\ell=2$ perturbations, even though sufficiently strong self-interactions are known to quench the radial instability of these stars. For solitonic boson stars, the bifurcations depend strongly on the gravitational coupling. As it decreases, a single family of spherical stars can have multiple zero modes, at which chains and rings alternate, and below a critical coupling the zero modes disappear. In flat spacetime, the rings still exist as static ring-like Q-balls, whereas no chains are found, which suggests that chains need gravity to exist.

title: Higher Order Component Attribution via Learned Surrogates in High Energy Physics
summary: Experimental High Energy Physics (HEP) has adopted the transformer architecture for identification of jets, particularly the state-of-the-art Particle Transformer (ParT) which injects explicit information about particle correlations into the attention mechanism. While able to achieve state-of-the-art results in accuracy, interpretability to its effectiveness has been limited. In this paper we propose component attribution methods using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) that directly tie back to the physical descriptors of jets, to probe whether mechanisms such as Multi-Head Attention (MHA), or the ParT architecture, are able to learn these as discriminating features.

title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
summary: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.

title: Experimental realization of twofold topological phase transition induced by long-range hoppings in one-dimensional chains
summary: Long-range hoppings offer a powerful mechanism to engineer exotic topological phases beyond conventional tight-binding models. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a twofold topological phase transition driven by third-nearest-neighbor couplings in a one-dimensional phononic chain that emulates cis-polyacetylene. Tunable hopping parameters in highly structured aluminum plates allow us to observe the emergence of Dirac points, a valley pseudospin structure, and topological edge states. The experimental results are supported by non-equilibrium Green's function transport calculations. Our findings confirm the predicted long-range phase diagram and establish phononic metamaterials as a versatile platform for exploring topological phenomena beyond the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger paradigm.

title: Discreetly Conformal: Higher-Order Chiral Scalars and the Discrete Series
summary: With its constant shift symmetry gauged, a massless scalar on two-dimensional flat space defines a conformal field theory whose classical phase space is equivalent to that of a chiral and an anti-chiral Floreanini--Jackiw scalar. We show that this picture generalizes: After gauging a larger set of the shift symmetries of the massless scalar field, it decomposes into a pair of generalized chiral and anti-chiral scalars, described by actions with higher-order spatial derivatives. We spell out their physical and gauge symmetries, and show how these give rise to the hidden conformal symmetry of the scalar with gauged shift symmetries. This lifts to de Sitter space, where we find that the discrete series scalars also decompose into these generalized chiral scalars, providing an explanation for their hidden conformal symmetry.

title: A pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in LISA data
summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a space-based gravitational wave detector scheduled for launch in the 2030s by the European Space Agency. Operating in the 0.1 mHz to 0.1 Hz band, LISA will observe a variety of astrophysical sources including but not limited to supermassive black hole mergers, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and white dwarf binaries. LISA will yield new insights, including supermassive black hole formation, new tests of general relativity, population studies of white dwarfs and others. Like all interferometric gravitational wave detectors, LISA data is expected to contain non-astrophysical transients, commonly referred to as glitches. We introduce a two step pipeline that consists of a search algorithm for detecting potential transients in simulated LISA data followed by a machine learning model that classifies the detected transients as gravitational waves or instrumental glitches. This is important for MBHBs with very high masses (around $10^6\ M_{\odot}$) which are transients that could be morphologically similar to LISA glitches in the data. Initial results demonstrate a promising ability to classify detected events with an accuracy close to $98\%$. The pipeline also shows the ability to analyze a month of data in under 2 minutes on a laptop. This shows an eventual utility of our pipeline for enabling accurate rapid alerts from low latency searches. It could also support model selection in global-fit analyses by providing an initial summary of the location and type of individual signals. This paper also discusses challenges encountered during training, including limitations of the current framework.

title: Production of hidden-charm molecular candidates with hidden strangeness in $B_s^0$ decays
summary: We study the production of spin-one $D_{s0}^*(2317)\bar D_s^*$, $D_{s1}(2460)\bar D_s^*$, and $D_{s1}(2536)\bar D_s^*$ molecular candidates in $B_s^0$ decays with an accompanying $η$, providing a complementary probe of their structure and production mechanisms. The meson-loop rescattering amplitudes are constructed from factorized weak sources and heavy-hadron chiral interactions. Constituent couplings are estimated using threshold-dependent compositeness relations, and the associated input uncertainties are propagated to the predicted rates. Opposite-$C$-parity partner hypotheses are included with inherited benchmark parameters. We calculate the branching fractions for two relative signs. Over the cutoff range $2\leqα\leq5$, the larger central branching fractions reach several $10^{-6}$ to several $10^{-5}$, suggesting potential accessibility in future experimental measurements.

title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
summary: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $μ\to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

title: Interacting particles crossing barriers: spatial statistics, choice of route taken and role of interactions
summary: We consider the statistics of pairs of particles moving in a potential energy landscape exhibiting a choice of different pathways from a local minimum start point to the global energy minimum destination. We examine the impact of both attractive and repulsive interactions between the particles, treating these via either a soft Gaussian or a Lennard-Jones potential. We investigate the statistics of which particle arrives at the destination first, arrival-time distributions and where in the system the second particle is located when the first arrives. We find that the typical arrival time of the first particle can be significantly different to that of a single particle, sometimes being much longer and in other cases being shorter, depending on the nature of the particle interactions. In the case of soft Gaussian attractive interactions, which effectively bind the pair of particles together to form a single larger particle, the arrival time can be much longer, since bigger particles cross barriers more slowly. In contrast, the arrival time is shorter when there is a repulsive core interaction between the particles, due to excluded-area and particle-ordering effects. We investigate the probability distribution of particles' positions through the Jensen--Shannon divergence which unveils the dependence of the spatial distribution of the particles within the confining potential on the parameters of the particle interaction potentials.

title: Analytic Bounds on Conformal Defect Spectra
summary: Conformal defects describe impurities and boundaries at criticality. Their stability depends on the scaling dimensions of operators localized on the defects, but these dimensions are often difficult to determine. We derive analytic upper bounds on the lowest nonvacuum scaling dimension using only two defect entropies and the dimension of a defect-changing operator. The bounds identify when relevant operators must appear on the defect with larger defect entropy. They follow from the conformal bootstrap of four-point functions of defect-changing operators and apply to unitary conformal line defects and to conformal boundaries in two-dimensional CFTs. The Ising and Potts models provide exact checks. In three-dimensional $O(N)$ models, we apply the bounds to direct sums of pinning field defects with symmetry-related orientations. Data from a single such defect exclude stable impurity order with three or more orientations in $O(2)$ and $O(3)$, or four or more in $O(4)$, for any geometry of the orientations, and require a relevant domain-wall operator between individually stable pinning field defects at every nonzero relative angle up to $120^\circ$ in $O(3)$ and up to $109.47^\circ$ in $O(4)$. A direct fuzzy-sphere computation of the lowest domain-wall dimension at different relative angles for $N=2,3,4$ is consistent with these bounds and indicates that, within this class of impurities, only two-state order remains a candidate for stable order in $O(3)$ and $O(4)$, while none survives in $O(2)$. A separate application to AdS/BCFT shows that, at fixed unequal brane tensions, a light boundary-condition-changing operator requires additional light primaries on the boundary with larger boundary entropy.

title: Landauer bound in a regular Bardeen black hole: extremality and evaporation
summary: Does the vanishing Hawking temperature of an extremal black hole imply that information can be erased without energy transfer? We investigate this question in the regular Bardeen geometry using a two-level quantum system, representing a quantum memory, coupled to a scalar bosonic field confined within an exterior cavity. The Hawking temperature tends to zero at extremality, as does the corresponding thermal Landauer scale. The field in an exterior cavity behaves differently, provided both walls remain away from the horizon, its lowest excitation energy stays finite. For a maximally mixed memory coupled to a reservoir initially in its unique ground state, we find $Q_\infty\geqΔ_{R,\infty}(1/2-ε)$, with $Δ_{R,\infty}$ the reservoir gap and $ε$ the reset error. For a resonant single-mode interaction, we give a reset protocol that attains the bound with no work supplied by the external control. In this example, the memory itself supplies the energy gained by the field. In the multimode calculation, counter-rotating terms are retained. Keeping the pulse parameters unchanged, we find a larger residual reset error closer to extremality. For reservoirs prepared thermally, we evaluate the Reeb--Wolf balance and find that the relative-entropy contribution, expressed in energy units, can have a finite low-temperature limit. These numerical preparations are externally imposed and remain hotter than the Hawking temperature. For comparison, an unconfined scalar field has near-extremal luminosity $P_\infty\propto y^4$, with $y=r_H/|g|-\sqrt2$. Assuming a particular quasistatic energy-loss prescription gives $y\propto t^{-1/2}$; this does not establish the existence of a stable remnant. For this particular reset operation, vanishing Hawking temperature therefore does not force the transferred heat to vanish.

title: An interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles
summary: We conjecture a novel interrelation of three neutrino mixing angles: $θ^{}_{23} = \left(θ^{}_{12} + θ^{}_{13}\right)/2 + π/8$, which predicts $θ^{}_{23} = 43.46^{+0.51^\circ}_{-0.52^\circ}$ with inputs of the latest JUNO and Daya Bay precision data. A simple ansatz is proposed to derive this phenomenologically favored and experimentally testable angle relation, and present a new expansion of the lepton flavor mixing matrix in powers of a single small parameter as a by-product.

title: Zak Phase, Pole--Zero Invariants and the Maslov Index of Bloch Cauchy Lines in One-Dimensional Periodic Media
summary: The topological properties of the Bloch bands of a one-dimensional periodic medium are described either by the Berry--Zak phase or by the poles and zeros of the surface impedance. We show that both can be read from one geometric object: the line spanned by the field and its flux (the Cauchy data) at an inversion centre. For each band, this line turns as the quasi-momentum runs over the Brillouin zone. Its number of turns, the Maslov index, is fixed by the parities (even or odd) of the Bloch functions at the two band edges, and its parity is the Zak phase. In a gap, the Cauchy line of the solution decaying on one side rotates monotonically with the energy, and an interface state between two crystals is a crossing of two such lines. This gives the known criterion of at most one state per gap in terms of the same lines. Examples with a stratified medium show that the choice of inversion centre changes the interface spectrum. The last section discusses what is missing to extend the construction to higher dimension.

title: Disentangling Multiple Scaling Dimensions via Operator Covariance in Critical Quantum Spin Systems
summary: We present a general proof of different power-law decays versus distance of the eigenvalues of two-point covariance matrices in critical lattice quantum models, allowing extraction of multiple scaling dimensions. We demonstrate the practical utility of this method in the context of a spin-1/2 chain with critical ground state described by the SU(2)_1 Wess--Zumino--Witten field theory. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute covariance matrices in different symmetry sectors, we resolve the expected relevant and marginal primary operators as well as some descendants. The covariance method can be integrated into many existing numerical schemes and promises to significantly enhance computational studies of quantum criticality.

title: Fermionic Kaluza-Klein Reductions
summary: We work out the Kaluza--Klein (KK) compactification on a general product spacetime for free spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 fields in arbitrary dimension. The analysis is performed at the level of the action, and the resulting lower-dimensional theory describes infinite towers of massive particles whose masses are related to the eigenvalues of the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators on the internal space. A Hodge-like decomposition is used to write down a KK ansatz for spin-3/2 fields, and the fate of gauge invariance is discussed.

title: Equatorial Periodic Orbits and Gravitational Wave Signatures in Weyl Geometric Gravity Black Holes
summary: Weyl geometric gravity theory is a gravitational theory with Lagrangian density constructed from the square of the Weyl curvature scalar and the strength of the Weyl vector. The theory can be reformulated as a scalar - vector - tensor theory in the Riemann geometry by introducing an auxiliary scalar field, in the presence of a non - minimal coupling between the Ricci scalar and the scalar field. Assuming that the Weyl vector has only a radial component, an exact spherically symmetric black hole type solution of the field equations in the vacuum can be obtained. The solution depends on three arbitrary integration constants. As compared to the case of the Schwarzschild black hole, the Weyl geometric gravity black hole solution contains two new terms, linear and quadratic, in the radial coordinate. It is the main goal of the present work to investigate astrophysical properties of the Weyl geometric black holes by considering the behavior of the timelike geodesics, which allows to explore how the geometric nonmetricity influences the strong-field dynamics of massive test particles as well as the topological structure of the periodic orbits. The resulting gravitational wave emission in extreme mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) systems is also considered. Our results show that the presence of nonmetricity in Weyl geometric gravity leaves distinct and measurable signatures on both the orbital topology and the emitted gravitational waveforms of compact EMRI systems. These unique temporal and amplitude modulations provide a promising observational avenue for testing the presence of nonmetricity on cosmic scales.

title: The ATAR, a dense and compact vertex detector for the PIONEER experiment
comment: 34th International Workshop on Vertex Detectors, Jul 20-24, 2026 in Stoss, Switzerland
summary: PIONEER is an approved experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institut (PSI) in Villigen, Switzerland that aims to measure the charged-pion branching ratio to electrons vs. muons with an accuracy of 0.01%. This is an order of magnitude improvement in precision compared to its predecessors and approaches the accuracy of the standard model prediction. The key elements of PIONEER are a high resolution calorimeter built concentrically around the high granularity active target (ATAR). The ATAR is composed of a stack of 48 low gain avalanche strip detectors (LGADs) to stop the beam pions and provide detailed information of the event topology. This will include precise timing (in the order of 200ps), spatial information (to an accuracy of about 60 micro meter) and pulse height information with a high dynamic range to separate pion stops from muons and MIPs. To avoid affecting the energy measurement of the positrons, the readout electronics is placed outside the acceptance angle of the calorimeter. It is composed of a fast amplifier and a fast sampling chip digitizing the LGAD wave form for real time analysis. The paper describes the PIONEER-experiment with focus on the ATAR and its readout. The status of the development and activities in 2026 will be reported.

title: Radiation principle for discrete acoustic equation on graphs with several cylindrical outlets to infinity
summary: A discrete analogue of the acoustic equation with a spectral parameter is studied on graphs with several cylindrical outlets to infinity. At infinity in each cylindrical outlet the coefficients of this equation converge exponentially fast to periodic functions. It is assumed that the spectral parameter is fixed and distinct from thresholds and flat bands. We construct a special basis of the continuous spectrum eigenfunctions (bounded solutions of the homogeneous equation that do not belong to l2), introduce the scattering matrix, and establish the radiation principle (a well-posed statement of the problem with radiation conditions at infinity).

title: Devitrification: crystal nucleation and growth mechanisms in glasses
summary: If a liquid is cooled rapidly, it may fall out of equilibrium before it can crystallize. It may, however, crystallize later from the nonequilibrium glassy state. Using the Random First-Order Transition (RFOT) theory of glasses, we discuss a variety of mechanisms of crystallization as a route to devitrification. Ordinary nucleation is sped up by the frozen in energy of the glass relative to the liquid. At sufficiently low temperatures, a mechanism of nanonucleation appears, producing nanometer scale crystal inclusions in the glass. Nanocrystallization depends strongly on the local fluctuations in stability, and the transition from classical nucleation and growth to nanocrystallization occurs dominantly through rare, less stable glassy regions that percolate through space, producing an additional dramatic speedup in the crystal nucleation and growth rates. Similar fluctuations in local stability also explain anomalies of crystal growth in deeply supercooled systems.

title: AdS to dS Flows Dual to Pseudo-Hermitian Theories
summary: We construct generalizations of ''centaur" geometries in more than two dimensions as solutions of Einstein gravity coupled to a ghost scalar. The solutions interpolate between asymptotically anti-de Sitter and asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes, with the two asymptotic regions separated by a horizon. A holographic interpretation is that they are dual to pseudo-Hermitian theories obtained from the continuation of real couplings and operators to purely imaginary values. One family of solutions is obtained from a supergravity theory that is a consistent truncation with a known embedding in string theory. We study the thermodynamic and linear stability of the solutions, and determine the uplift of the supergravity solutions to eleven dimensions.

title: Weak-field analytical solutions for f(R,L_matt) gravity in a static and spherically symmetric space-time for perfect fluids
summary:
We study the weak-field regime of $f(R,\lmatt)$ gravity for a static and spherically symmetric configuration described by a perfect fluid, whose energy density is perturbed about a constant reference value. By means of a weak-field limit expansion about a Minkowski geometric background and under a quasi-Newtonian approximation, we derive and analytically solve the coupled system that governs the gravitational perturbations and the matter variables.
  The solution contains the long-range Newtonian contribution and Yukawa-type corrections in the temporal and radial components of the metric. In the matter sector, the energy density, the internal energy, and the pressure acquire radial contributions, with a non-zero constant background rest-mass energy density and vanishing background internal energy and pressure. The results show how the non-minimal coupling between curvature and matter jointly modifies the geometry and the fluid in the considered regime.

title: The PICO-40L detector
summary: The PICO collaboration has designed and constructed a novel bubble chamber to search for evidence of Weakly Interacting Massive Particles, a leading dark matter candidate. The PICO-40L detector is the successor to PICO-60, and uses a fully redesigned system for pressurization of the active volume after a bubble nucleation event. Pressure in PICO-40L is transferred to the target fluid through a set of two nested synthetic quartz vessels connected by bellows below the active volume. This is in contrast to the design of earlier detectors in which the pressure was transferred through a buffer fluid atop the target fluid, within a single synthetic quartz vessel connected to a bellows above the active volume. Removing the buffer fluid removes the potential for backgrounds arising from the interface between the two fluids, and moving the bellows below the target fluid suppresses potential backgrounds from particulates originating from the bellows. The newly designed detector concept of PICO-40L is referred to as the Right-Side-Up (RSU) design and requires a dedicated thermal system to keep the lower region of the detector cold while the upper region is stably superheated. The main goal of PICO-40L is to establish the performance characteristics of the RSU detector concept, which will inform the operating configuration of the final generation PICO dark matter detector, PICO-500, which is currently under construction at SNOLAB. This paper reviews the design, installation, and performance of the PICO-40L detector.

title: Absence of Excited Bound States for All Fibers of the Fröhlich Polaron at Weak Coupling
summary: We study the discrete spectrum of the three-dimensional Fröhlich polaron at weak coupling and fixed total momentum. We prove that, for sufficiently small coupling and every total momentum $0<|ξ|\le 1/4$, the ground-state eigenvalue is the only eigenvalue below the essential spectrum. Our proof builds on the analogous zero-momentum result of Seiringer (2023). Combined with that result and the work of Dahlbaek (2017), this implies that, at sufficiently weak coupling, no fiber Hamiltonian has a discrete excited eigenvalue.

title: Thirty years of 2D MIT
summary: The zero-magnetic-field metal-insulator transition in strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems was experimentally discovered three decades ago, thereby triggering extensive experimental and theoretical investigations. Prior to this discovery, the occurrence of such a transition --- as well as the very existence of a metallic phase in two dimensions --- was regarded as forbidden within the framework of the one-parameter scaling theory of localization. In this work, we provide a comprehensive review of the transport and thermodynamic properties of two-dimensional electron and hole systems in which carrier-carrier interactions constitute the dominant energy scale. We present and critically analyze both experimental observations and theoretical developments accumulated over the past thirty years.

title: Density kernel and temporal quantum information probes in double-scaled SYK
summary: Entanglement is conventionally defined through a Hilbert space bipartition on a fixed time slice. Recent work has generalized this notion to multiple times through a non-Hermitian density kernel constructed from temporal correlation functions, encoding causal response, temporal non-classicality and quantum dynamics. We construct this kernel in the double-scaled Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (DSSYK) model using its exact chord Hilbert space formulation and study the resulting temporal information diagnostics. The direct sum structure of chord space naturally introduces a coarse-graining under which coherence between different chord sectors is removed. We show that the corresponding kernel measures quantify how information is dynamically transferred across subregions in the chord Hilbert space. We find that decreasing $λ$ enhances the propagation of temporal correlation across chord sectors, as well as the loss of memory within a fixed sector. This accelerated temporal dynamics in the small $λ$ limit coincides with the emergence of a semiclassical gravity description. Depending on the chord space partition, the probes exhibit either saturation, a growth followed by a decay, or temporary memory loss. The characteristic propagation time is nicely captured by a wavefront picture in Krylov space, with position-dependent hopping parameters that are determined by the DSSYK Lanczos coefficients. Finally, given the quantum sine-dilaton gravity description of DSSYK and its connections to de Sitter holography, our results provide a controlled setting for probing temporal quantum correlations across quantum and semiclassical gravitational regimes, and motivate a geometric interpretation of the density kernel.

title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
comment: 42 pages, 2 figures. Presents part of the results of arXiv:2609.25477, with an improved treatment of the regularity conditions and of the field equations
summary: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalize the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including a general axial condition that allows for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behavior of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.

title: Possible Solution to the Gallium Anomaly? Nuclear Transition Densities
summary: The gallium anomaly, a 20% deficit in the measured $ν_e$ captures on $^{71}$Ga, remains unexplained. A recent work [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 131805 (2026), arXiv:2512.20560] has proposed a solution based on the breakdown of the factorization of lepton and nuclear wavefunctions that underlies the prediction of the cross section, combined with ad hoc Gamow-Teller nuclear transition densities. We test this proposed solution with transition densities calculated within the nuclear shell model (NSM), normalized to the $^{71}$Ge electron-capture half-life and convolved with Dirac-Hartree-Fock-Slater electron wavefunctions. We explore several NSM interactions, bare and effective Gamow-Teller operators, as well as the impact of the valence space. In all cases, we obtain remarkably consistent NSM transition densities. Our factorized and nonfactorized cross sections agree, remaining 20% higher than the measured value. In addition, we use NSM single-nucleon transition densities as ansatz and find that solving the anomaly requires fine-tuned densities, with percent-level cancellations and an overall scale orders of magnitude larger than the calculated NSM ones. We conclude that the gallium anomaly is not solved when using realistic nuclear transition densities.

title: Finite-strain second-gradient elasticity with an energetic surface: existence of minimizers, incremental theory and elastocapillary beading
summary: We develop a finite-strain theory of second-gradient elasticity for solids with a material surface endowed with its own constitutive energy. The bulk second gradient plays two complementary roles. First, under suitable coercivity assumptions and convexity with respect to the second gradient, we prove the existence of minimizers for nonnegative, lower semicontinuous surface energy densities, without requiring convexity, polyconvexity, positive one-homogeneity, or an upper growth bound on the surface energy. Second, it introduces an intrinsic bulk length scale that affects the onset of instability and wavelength selection. To investigate these effects, we derive an incremental small-on-large formulation in the finitely deformed configuration and apply it to the elastocapillary beading of an axially stretched soft cylinder. For an infinite cylinder and the parameters considered, increasing the second-gradient modulus delays bifurcation and shifts the critical mode towards longer wavelengths. Above a finite threshold of this modulus, the critical stretch saturates in the long-wave limit. The model is implemented in the open-source finite element code OOFEM using C1-continuous isogeometric analysis. Finite-cylinder simulations yield onset stretches in close agreement with the analytical predictions. Selected post-bifurcation branches traced by arc-length continuation exhibit beaded states and supercritical bifurcation at small second-gradient moduli, whereas larger moduli are associated with subcritical bifurcation and the formation of distinct thick and thin segments.

title: Jackknife-conformal uncertainty for linear ACE potentials: calibrated forces and silicon properties compared with Bayesian and POPS baselines
summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials are misspecified, so Bayesian posterior variances understate their errors. For linear atomic cluster expansion (ACE) potentials we derive calibrated uncertainties from one misspecification-robust parameter covariance, the delete-one-configuration jackknife. Scaled by one conformal quantile from a held-out part of the training set, it gives per-atom force uncertainties close to their target coverage on held-out silicon data and on cracks left out of the fit; screw dislocations left out are under-covered by the smaller of the two models. With one scale fitted to the forces of a held-out test split, the same parameter distribution is propagated to 21 properties of silicon, from elastic constants to defect and surface energies, by implicit differentiation through each relaxation and by committees, and is tested against density functional theory (DFT) without tuning on any property. For a smaller and a larger model the intervals cover most properties, and the larger model's are about 4 times tighter. The Bayesian posterior with one calibrated scale has the wrong shape: it covers fewer properties and has far lower joint evidence. Pointwise optimal parameter sets (POPS), once their hypercube is numerically defined, performs comparably on the properties, but its per-atom force regions are not calibrated to a target (0.95 and 0.84 at a nominal 0.90). Where the jackknife fails is relaxed point defects, whose training cells are all hot snapshots: a bias that every configuration shares is invisible to a jackknife, but it can be measured from the training labels, and as a discrepancy term, devised after the property results were seen, it brings the coverage close to nominal.

title: Reflecting Baths and Black Hole Interior Islands in JT Gravity
comment: 45 pages, 5 figures; comments and references are welcome
summary: We study the evolution of entanglement entropy within the island prescription in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to finite non-gravitating baths bounded by reflecting walls. For free massless Dirac matter, we study the evolution of entanglement entropy, explicitly accounting for correlations induced by the reflecting boundaries. For sufficiently short baths, the no-island entropy saturates below the thermodynamic black hole entropy, avoiding the usual information paradox associated with its unbounded growth. For larger baths, reflected correlations drive the exterior quantum extremal surface toward the future horizon, leading to a temporary disappearance of the the near-horizon exterior island branch. We find that this branch first appears at a scrambling-like scale, and it reappears at a time that is proportional to the size of the bath. We extend the extremization across the horizon using regular Kruskal coordinates and identify real quantum extremal surfaces in the black hole interior. We show that, in the parameter regime studied, interior island configurations provide the dominant contribution to the radiation entropy during the exterior disappearance time interval, resolving the reappearance of the information paradox in an exterior-only description.

title: The Weyl Tensor for Gravitational-Wave Causal Sets: Thickness of Geodesic Analogs and Geodesic Deviation
summary: Causal set theory proposes that spacetime is replaced by a partially ordered set (a directed acyclic graph) at the smallest scales. This graph is postulated to produce all the features of continuous geometry above some discreteness scale. We develop an approach to sprinkling causal sets into a linearized plane gravitational wave spacetime, and report on the feasibility of using the analog of geodesic deviation to find a component of the Weyl tensor for such causal sets. We take the collection of all longest chains between a pair of elements to be the discrete analog of the timelike geodesic between them and find through numerical simulations in Minkowski spacetime of various dimensions that the spread or "thickness" of the collection increases with chain length. We estimate, assuming an ideal element-to-element spatial distance estimator and a wave of amplitude $h_0 = 10^{-2}$, that at least $N_{\mathrm{total}} \gtrsim \mathcal{O}(10^8)$ elements are needed to overcome the noise introduced by the thickness and detect the curvature. This is beyond the $\mathcal{O}(10^6)$ elements we can currently simulate. Future work may show ways of extracting more information from the sprinkled causal set and hence lowering the estimate for $N_{\mathrm{total}}$.

title: A scalable computational framework for PDEs on physical networks
summary: Transport, reaction and wave propagation on physical networks depend on dynamics along edges and interactions at junctions. We present a flexible framework for modeling physical networks at scale. A network calculus expresses edge dynamics and vertex contributions as fields over the whole network. Differential operators satisfy integration by parts-identities that connect local dynamics to global conservation laws, and explicit vertex constraints allow a variety of physical junction conditions. We implement this formalism using the open-source Dedalus spectral framework. This accommodates heterogeneous edge lengths, material properties and spectral resolutions. Initial-value, boundary-value and eigenvalue problems share a parallel solution method that eliminates internal unknowns independently on subgraphs and couples their solutions through shared boundary vertex interfaces. We verify numerical convergence and demonstrate strong and weak scaling on networks with millions of edges. We present applications to localized optical resonances in photonic networks, preferential channel formation during mineral replacement in evolving pore networks, and nonlinear dispersive waves for KdV on a periodic network.

title: Analytical mean-field model for electrochemical metallization memristors with a nanoporous matrix: application to Ag/anodic alumina/Al
summary: Memristors based on electrochemical metallization with many filaments are usually modeled by microscopic simulations with many parameters or by phenomenological laws whose parameters are hard to relate to physical quantities. We present an analytical mean-field model for a population of Ag filaments confined in the pores of a nanoporous matrix, built on Ohm's law, Faraday's law and a power-based rupture criterion. The filaments have a truncated normal distribution of cross-sections and rupture leaving lognormally distributed gaps whose median grows with the dissipated power. Gap closing shifts the distribution of squared gaps rigidly, and the model therefore admits closed-form expressions for the switching voltage, the read current, the rupture branch and the high-voltage current. We apply it to Ag/nanoporous anodic alumina/Al structures fabricated from industrial-grade aluminum, with a 2.4$μ$m alumina layer, and measured under ambient conditions. The parameters were fitted to the bipolar sweeps, with the gap dispersion taken from the temporal shape of the read after a pulse. They reproduce the bipolar response, including voltage-controlled negative differential resistance, and predict without refitting the unipolar sweeps and the amplitude of the pulse response, where state memory appears. A second sample, with a larger contact deposited chemically, is described by the same model. In vacuum the devices neither switch nor show negative differential resistance, as expected if adsorbed water supplies the counter reaction; the residual high-voltage current follows ionic hopping conduction.

title: A Song of Spice and Ice: A diagonal dual to dS$_3$ & its Galilean flat space limit
summary:
We propose a diagonal CFT dual to asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes in three dimensions (3d), constructed from the holomorphic part of the CFT dual at the future boundary and the antiholomorphic part of the CFT dual at the past boundary, in part inspired by an antipodal map between the two CFT copies. This gives equal and opposite imaginary central charges for the holomorphic and antiholomorphic sectors. The corresponding diagonal holographic energy-momentum tensor expectation values are constructed from the Wavefunction at the future boundary and its conjugate. This enables a recovery of the entropy of $dS_3$, as well as a family of complex Kerr $dS_3$ spacetimes with two real horizons, by a Cardy formula.
  We then explore the flatspace limit of our dS construction. With the central charges as above, the flatspace limit naturally induces a Galilean contraction on the dual diagonal 2d CFT, in contrast to the more familiar Carrollian limit when 3d Asymptotically Flat Spacetime (AFS) is approached from $AdS_3$. The corresponding limit for the complex Kerr family above leaves the inner horizon intact, resulting in flat space complex black holes ($\mathbb{C}$BH) that are closely related to flat space cosmologies which arise from BTZ black holes in AdS$_3$. We recover the entropy of these $\mathbb{C}$BHs by the BMS-Cardy formula.

title: Axion cloud survival in nuclear star clusters
summary: Stellar perturbations can ionize a superradiant boson cloud while transferring energy and angular momentum from the perturbing orbits. We follow the cloud after superradiant saturation by coupling its occupation to a two-dimensional, orbit-averaged Fokker--Planck equation for the stars. The evolution includes stellar relaxation, capture, orbital backreaction, and gravitational-wave (GW) emission from both the cloud and the stellar orbits. We evolve 24 models with black hole masses $M=10^5$--$10^7M_{\odot}$ and couplings $0.04\leqα\leq0.40$. Stars with semimajor axes of a few Bohr radii, $r_c=M/α^2$, dominate ionization. Stellar replenishment from the outer cluster sustains ionization over hundreds of Myr, particularly for extended clouds. Of the 24 models, 21 lose at least $99\%$ of their initial cloud mass. For compact clouds, intrinsic GW emission dominates the depletion.

title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-filled $3$-manifolds along fundamental shadow link complements with big volume
summary: We prove the Volume Conjecture and the Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for closed oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn-fillings along a fundamental shadow link complement, provided that their volumes are sufficiently close to that of the complement. More generally, we show that the conjectured asymptotic expansions hold for pairs obtained by change-of-pair operations on a fundamental shadow link complement whenever the volume of the corresponding hyperbolic cone manifold is sufficiently close to that of the complement. A key ingredient in the proof is the introduction of extended quantum $6j$-symbols and a Weak Reflection Symmetry satisfied by them. The Weak Reflection Symmetry is established by relating the extended quantum $6j$-symbols to the $b$-$6j$ symbols through a real Gevrey-$1$ estimate and a truncated Borel-Laplace transform.

title: Ion Redistribution and Lattice-Distortion-Modulated d-Electron Correlation in Layered Multiferroic ABP$_2$S$_6$ Probed by X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy
summary: Ferroelectric phase transitions are driven by ion displacement-induced symmetry breaking, yet their chemical signatures are rarely probed directly at the atomic level. Here, we establish temperature-dependent X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) as a powerful and quantitative probe of ferroelectric phase transitions by tracking ion migration-induced changes in local chemical environments. Using van der Waals (vdW) layered ABP$_2$S$_6$ materials as a model system, we systematically compare CuCrP$_2$S$_6$ (CCPS), which undergoes a ferroelectric phase transition, with AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ (ACPS), which remains paraelectric over the same temperature range. While ACPS exhibits only smooth trivial thermal broadening and shifts in core-level spectra, CCPS shows pronounced and enormously large temperature-dependent XPS anomalies across the ferroelectric transition, demonstrating that XPS is intrinsically sensitive to ferroelectric order. Detailed analysis of the Cu 2p spectra reveals that these anomalies originate from temperature-driven Cu$^+$ ion migration associated with polarization switching, whereas concurrent changes in the Cr core levels reflect secondary lattice squeezing and modulation of d-electron correlation induced by Cu displacement. Supported by a ferroelectric structural model, we further correlate XPS binding-energy shifts with the magnitude of Cu-ion migration, enabling a quantitative estimation of ionic displacement directly from spectroscopic observables. This work also highlights the rich information provided by temperature-dependent XPS for detecting and quantifying ferroelectric phase transitions and ion migration, offering a general chemical probe for ferroic materials and ion-displacement-driven phase transitions.

title: Dressed AdS$_4$ black holes in M-theory from the 3d superconformal index
summary: The superconformal index of 4d $\mathcal N\,{=}\,4$ SYM has been shown to exhibit a rich phase structure, whose holographic interpretation in AdS$_5$ involves (dual-)dressed black holes, gray galaxies, and graviton gas contributions. Here we extend the analysis to 3d CFTs, focusing on ABJM theory and the $\mathcal N=4$ ADHM theory. We study the microcanonical superconformal index with two independent charges at finite $N$ and obtain exact signed state degeneracies up to large charges. The results exhibit the black hole physics expected to emerge at large-$N$, including isolated black holes and black holes dressed by additional matter.

title: Optical Geometry of a Lorentz-Violating BTZ-Like Black Hole: Reflection Double and Dirac Scattering
summary: We analyze the optical geometry of a static BTZ-like black-hole metric with a Lorentz-violating radial factor, distinguishing the one-sided black-hole exterior from the reflection double constructed from its optical spatial section. The optical metric is ultrastatic and has constant negative Gaussian curvature. The reflection double is smooth and complete, with a minimal circle; it is a geometric completion, not a demonstrated solution of the Einstein--bumblebee equations. We derive exact criteria for null-geodesic crossing and return, evaluate the corresponding angular sweeps, and determine the finite domain of a Euclidean surface-of-revolution embedding. Two inequivalent magnetic configurations are specified as external test fields on the embeddable patch. For a continuum graphene analogue on the doubled geometry, we derive the covariant massless Dirac operator and reduce its radial equation to Scarf-II partner equations. The full-line connection problem yields flux-normalized complex scattering amplitudes and probabilities, the resonance-pole lattice and its gamma-function residues, spectral widths and quality factors, the digamma Wigner delay, and conditional pole contributions to packet dynamics. We compare the analytic amplitudes with direct numerical integration of the radial partner equation, including their complex phases. We further separate fixed-$\ell$ from fixed-$Λ_e$ parameter protocols and audit the optical effective-mass degeneracy using Lorentzian curvature invariants, timelike geodesics, and a massive Klein--Gordon probe. Throughout, the gravitational completion, prescribed fields, and continuum scattering results are interpreted only within the scope of their respective constructions. Device-level graphene transport and a self-consistent gravitational wormhole require additional physical input.

title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
summary: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.

title: Bichromatic light-induced electronic torques on the Néel vector in Rashba magnetic multipoles from $p$-wave magnets to $i$-wave altermagnets
summary: Light can control magnetic order on ultrafast timescales, but for a two-dimensional magnet with an out-of-plane order parameter $\boldsymbol N\parallel\hat z$, the inverse Faraday field is collinear with $\boldsymbol N$ and gives no transverse torque. Here we show that bichromatic $(ω,bω)$ light generates electronic torques perpendicular to $\boldsymbol N$ in Rashba-coupled magnetic multipoles, from $p$-wave ($n=1$) magnets to $i$-wave ($n=6$) altermagnets. Beyond high-frequency effective fields, we evaluate the exact Floquet response and the generalized torque per occupied electron, for prescribed occupations. The momentum-dependent exchange terms dominate this Fermi-sea torque and remove the leading-order zeros (amplitude-ratio blindspots) of the momentum-independent field in the channels tested. For out-of-plane $\boldsymbol N$, rotational symmetry permits a transverse torque only if $\gcd(n,b+1)=1$ for counter-rotating beams or $\gcd(n,b-1)=1$ for co-rotating beams. For in-plane $\boldsymbol N$, the Fermi sea also gives a torque component along $\hat z$ that the momentum-independent field cannot produce. We classify the active channels, with $n=1,\dots,6$ and $b=1,\dots,7$, by frequency scaling and origin (cycle-averaged versus oscillating exchange). As a control, a Rashba ferromagnet ($n=0$) has one symmetry-allowed out-of-plane channel and a weak in-plane response without a selection rule. Finite-momentum occupied-state physics is therefore essential for light-driven torques in unconventional magnets, and the exact Floquet calculation validates and extends the high-frequency description.

title: NLO corrections to charged-current correlators near extremality: non-Abelian hydrodynamics meets AdS$_2$
comment: 56 pages plus appendix, comments are welcome
summary: We analytically compute the longitudinal charged-current correlator in a near-extremal holographic plasma with quark and isospin chemical potentials, $μ_q$ and $μ_3$ respectively. To this end, we study fluctuations of gauge fields around a low-temperature AdS$_5$ Reissner-Nordström black hole charged both under the quark number and the isospin. The result is obtained at next-to-leading order in a hydrodynamic expansion where apart from the temperature and isospin chemical potential, the frequency and momenta are small compared to the quark chemical potential, $ω,k,T,μ_3\llμ_q$. This approach captures the interplay between the hydrodynamic-like pole and the tower of infrared modes produced by the AdS$_2$ throat controlling the geometry of the black hole near extremality. At zero isospin chemical potential, the resulting quasinormal-mode formula reproduces the collision of the diffusive pole with the infrared spectrum, while the finite isospin chemical potential lifts this collision. The analytic spectrum agrees precisely with the full numerical results. The next-to-leading-order correlator also substantially improves the spectral function beyond the standard hydrodynamic regime $ω,k,μ_3\ll T$, extending the agreement with numerics to larger frequencies and momenta.

title: Quasinormal modes of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole: Linear stability and strong cosmic censorship conjecture
comment: 34 pages, 5 tables, 10 figures. SS, SG, AC, CS, and SMD contributed equally to this work and should be considered joint first authors
summary: We present an alternative formulation of coupled gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations of Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black holes, yielding decoupled radial and angular equations with a well-defined $Λ\rightarrow 0$ limit. We compute the quasinormal mode spectra using spectral and direct integration methods, finding excellent agreement. All of these modes are consistent with the linear stability of the Kerr--Newman--de Sitter black hole. We investigate the photon sphere and near-extremal modes, revealing a non-trivial interplay between rotation and electric charge. We further explore the implications for the strong cosmic censorship conjecture and find that the photon sphere modes predominantly determine its validity within the parameter space considered. While increasing the rotation of the black hole generally favours the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, increasing the electric charge can promote its violation. We also find that the region of parameter space exhibiting a violation of the conjecture is comparatively smaller for gravitational perturbations than for electromagnetic perturbations. These results highlight the important role of rotation, electric charge, and the nature of perturbations in determining the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture in Kerr--Newman--de Sitter spacetimes.

title: Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients
summary: We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.

title: Growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb quantum devices
summary: We report recent progress in the growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb Majorana devices for three-terminal correlation experiments. A critical prerequisite for these devices is a continuous Pb film spanning from the PbTe nanowire to the substrate. In previous studies, PbTe nanowires were spatially separated from the substrate mask, making them unable to fulfill this requirement. To address this issue, we have developed a new growth and fabrication approach. Key fabrication steps are introduced between the PbTe growth and Pb deposition. The top facet of the PbTe nanowire is covered with a Te capping layer before breaking the ultra-high vacuum, enabling ex situ processing for subsequent steps. The mask is then removed, followed by the fabrication of shadow walls. After reloading the chip into the growth chamber, the Te protection layer is removed through thermal decomposition, and the Pb film is subsequently deposited.
